thread:
alice: Quick check-in — I ran a short canary for the "soft-wait" batch stabilizer on a single serving pool. Goal: reduce p95 token latency spikes during microbursts while keeping throughput high. Results below, need eyes and ideas.

ben: summary numbers please?

alice: baseline (no stabilizer): p50=8ms/token, p95=120ms/token, p99=310ms/token, avg throughput 520 tok/s per GPU. With soft-wait(hold=1.5ms, jitter=0.6ms): p50=9ms, p95=78ms, p99=210ms, throughput 498 tok/s. KV hit rate dropped from 87% -> 82% in the first 10m.

carla: interesting. did kernel selection change at all? any fallback to fp16-optimized kernels?

alice: good question — profiler shows no kernel switch. Same code path. The observed perf shift correlates with slightly different sequence-length batching (more mixed lengths), which affects KV cache priming.

dmitri: can you paste the config you used?

alice: sure:

```
soft_wait:
  enabled: true
  hold_ms: 1.5
  jitter_ms: 0.6
  token_budget_target: 64
  allow_hedge: true
  hedge_threshold_tokens: 512
```

ben: token_budget_target=64 is lower than our usual 128 — were you trying to prioritize latency?

alice: yes, smaller target to keep microbatches small. It reduced p95 but we lost some KV reuse. The profiler flamegraph shows more short-lived KV entries and slightly higher eviction churn.

carla: do we have request arrival histograms? are these microbursts dominated by many short requests or a few long ones?

alice: arrival histogram attached in logs (pasted snapshot): burst mode = lots of 8-40 token requests arriving in <4ms windows. So coalescing them into larger batches helps amortize kernel overhead but increases token latency for earliest requests. Soft-wait seems to smooth that.

dmitri: hypothesis: soft-wait jitter increases inter-arrival mixing, which increases sequence-length variance in a batch and reduces KV prefix hits. Could test by adjusting token_budget_target up and hold_ms down.

alice: I tried token_budget_target=96 with hold_ms=1.0ms, jitter=0.4ms — p95=85ms, p99=230ms, KV hit 85%, throughput 510 tok/s. So middle ground looks promising.

ben: any kernel-level contention? profiler -> GPU kernel queues?

alice: profiler shows slightly higher occupancy variance but no obvious kernel slowdowns. The extra latency seems mostly queuing + KV cache miss overhead (memory lookups).

carla: worth checking cache priming heuristics — maybe we can bias batch formation to preserve contiguous prefixes when possible. Eg prefer coalescing same-conversation requests or same-seed prefixes within 2ms window.

dmitri: we could introduce a tiny prefix affinity score in the queue: +weight if prefix hash matches hot set. Implementation: keep small LRU of prefix hashes; when forming batch, prefer requests with matching hash up to budget. Should be cheap.

alice: good idea. Could help KV hit without increasing hold time. But needs measurable test — I can prototype in the queue sampler.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for ./runtime/soft-wait-affinity v0.1 on pool eu-west-1-a (3 nodes).

bob: (not in participants) — adding quick note: watch tail p999 too. sometimes p99 looks ok but p999 shows pathological outliers for long requests.

alice: noted — I'll capture p999 and kernel-level timings next run. Also plan to add a microbenchmark: synthetic traffic with controllable arrival bursts and sequence-length distribution to isolate variables.

carla: action items?

alice: 1) prototype prefix-affinity sampler (me) 2) run param sweep: token_budget_target in [64,96,128], hold_ms in [0.6,1.0,1.5], jitter in [0.2,0.6,1.0] (ben + me) 3) capture detailed p999 and KV eviction traces (dmitri) 4) if results look good, canary soft-wait-affinity v0.1 (deploy-bot)

ben: timeline?

alice: aim for sweep today/overnight, preliminary numbers tomorrow morning. I'll post concise table.

dmitri: I'll add a flamegraph diffs script to the perf repo so we can compare runs automatically.

carla: sounds good. If prefix-affinity gives >3% KV hit improvement without throughput loss, we can adopt as default.

alice: cool — will update thread with results. :thumbsup:
